Former Site Manager Convicted and Imprisoned for Demanding Kickbacks from Migrant Workers

11 November 2026 Foreign manpower
Koh Kim Sia, a former site manager at 800 Super Waste Management Pte Ltd, has been convicted under the Employment of Foreign Manpower Act (EFMA) for demanding kickbacks, or payments from five migrant workers as a condition for their continued employment with the company. He was sentenced to 49 days of imprisonment.

2 Koh faced a total of 24 charges under the EFMA for demanding kickbacks as a condition for their employment or continued employment. He pleaded guilty to five charges involving five migrant workers.

Advisory

Demanding or receiving employment kickbacks from migrant workers is a serious offence, and carries a fine of up to $30,000, imprisonment for up to two years, or both, per charge.
